key_insight: RiVER shows that LLMs can be trained effectively on score-based tasks without ground-truth answers by turning execution feedback into calibrated, ranking-aware rewards.
engineering_relevance: This enables reinforcement learning for coding and optimization problems where exact solutions are unavailable, while still improving general coding performance on standard benchmarks.
method: Use deterministic execution scores as continuous rewards instead of ground-truth labels.
Apply instance-wise reward calibration to avoid scale dominance across tasks.
Emphasize top-ranked solutions to reduce frequency dominance from repeatedly sampled weak candidates.
evidence_signal: Trained on 12 AtCoder Heuristic Contest tasks, RiVER improved ALE rating rank by 8.9% for Qwen3-8B and 9.4% for GLM-Z1-9B-0414, and transferred to exact-solution benchmarks with average gains of 2.4% on LiveCodeBench and 3.5% on USACO.
watch_item: Performance depends on stable score calibration and task-specific execution feedback; poorly designed reward shaping may still bias updates or reduce transfer.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
